c.tagline: Basque reinvention — Guggenheim titanium, old-town pintxos, green hills.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; Uber presence is limited, so licensed street/rank taxis and the Cabify and Bolt apps are the norm. An airport supplement applies.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Casco Viejo and on transit

hood_desc: Bilbao's medieval old town — the Siete Calles (Seven Streets), Santiago Cathedral, arcaded Plaza Nueva and the covered Ribera Market. A walkable maze of pintxos bars and shops, lively day and night; best for first-timers who want atmosphere and the classic txikiteo bar-hop.

The elegant 19th-century modern centre on the west bank, home to the Guggenheim Museum, the Zubizuri footbridge, grand Gran Via shopping and Abando station. Wide avenues, upscale hotels and easy transport make it a calm, convenient first-time base, especially for families.

A busy commercial district beside Abando around Plaza Indautxu and the Azkuna Zentroa (Alhondiga) cultural centre, with the Fine Arts Museum and Dona Casilda park nearby. Packed with shops, restaurants and the lively 'Pozas' bar street — good for shopping and going out.

The gritty-turned-hip quarter across the river from Casco Viejo — Bilbao's bohemian, multicultural core of street art, galleries, vintage shops and buzzing bars. San Frantzisko is also the city's LGBT hub. Best for younger travellers after an alternative, going-out scene.

A student neighbourhood across the Nervion around the University of Deusto, with riverside promenades, green space and everyday local prices. Well connected by metro yet away from the tourist crush — a relaxed, budget-friendly base.

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.hours: The metro runs about 6am-11pm on weekdays, until 2am on Fridays and all night on Saturdays; night Gautxori buses cover the small hours on other nights.
transit.pay: Get a rechargeable Barik card (about EUR 3) from metro machines and top it up; a single Barik metro ride is roughly EUR 0.90-1.80 by zone, versus EUR 1.80-2.60 for a paper single. The same Barik card works on Metro Bilbao, the Euskotren tram, Bilbobus, Bizkaibus and the Artxanda funicular, and contactless bank-card tap-in is rolling out.

ferry: Port of Bilbao (Brittany Ferries to Portsmouth, UK)

transit.m: Bizkaibus A3247 to Bilbao centre/Termibus (~25 min, every 15-20 min)

tip.r: Round up or leave 5-10% for good service; not obligatory.
